key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics, energy storage, and low-power computing must be co-designed to make edge AI practical and sustainable.
engineering_relevance: The paper highlights (anti)ferroelectrics as promising materials to simultaneously improve local energy harvesting, electrostatic storage, and in-memory neuromorphic computing for distributed intelligence.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence
Map emerging material capabilities against power and storage needs
Argue for co-creation of harvesting, storage, and computing devices
evidence_signal: This is a perspective paper, so its support comes from a requirements-and-gap analysis of the state of indoor photovoltaics and low-power computing rather than new experimental benchmarking.
watch_item: A key implementation challenge is whether available materials can reliably meet the combined efficiency, storage, and device-integration demands of real edge computing systems.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
